name: Arrakeen
note: Fan work. Dune belongs to the Herbert estate; nothing from any book, film or game is used, and every shape here is this project's own geometry built from the description. The basin, the Shield Wall, the dune sea and the city are generated by tools/make-arrakeen.py. Positions are [lat, lon] against an origin in the middle of the city, which on a world with no agreed prime meridian is as good a datum as any.
attribution: Arrakeen is fan work: geometry generated by tools/make-arrakeen.py. No book, film or game assets used.

districts._: [name, hex colour, base height, tallest, box as [lat south, lon west, lat north, lon east]]

landmarks.name: The Residency
landmarks.info: The great house of whoever holds the fief. Thick-walled, blind to the outside, and built round a garden of a few hundred square metres of green - which on a world that would drink a man dry is not decoration but a statement about who controls the water.

landmarks.name: The Great Windtrap
landmarks.info: The city's lung. A scoop the size of a cathedral standing into the prevailing wind, with precipitators inside it that pull the little water the air carries out of it. Every roof in Arrakeen has a small one; this is the one that fills the public cisterns.

landmarks.name: The Landing Field
landmarks.info: The only way anything arrives. The Guild's lighters come down from a heighliner in orbit, stand on the fused rock while they are unloaded, and go back up; nothing else on this planet is that tall or that clean.

landmarks.name: Sietch Tabr
landmarks.info: From the outside it is a rock with nothing on it, which is the entire design. What is inside it is a town of several thousand people, and the water they have been putting away for generations.

landmarks.name: The Shield Wall
landmarks.info: The rampart that makes the basin habitable: it keeps the coriolis storms and the great worms off Arrakeen, and everything that lives here lives in its lee. The road out to the deep desert goes through the one gap in it.

landmarks.name: The Funeral Plain
landmarks.info: Open dune, south-west past the last rock. The ranks run with the wind and they move: what is drawn here is where they were.

life._: a windtrap on every roof, dew collectors on the parapets, awnings over the lanes, and ornithopters over the basin

desert._: the spice works out past the last rock, and the sign of what comes up underneath it
